answer.decision: Use staged canaries with automatic abort thresholds, feature-flag control, and backward-compatible additive schema changes.
answer.action: Start with a 1% traffic canary for at least 12 minutes, then expand through regional stages to global traffic within one business day if healthy. Automatically stop promotion and disable the new routing path when error rate approaches 1% or p95 latency breaches the approved regression threshold; roll back the application version when database read-pattern signals regress. Keep additive schema fields in place during rollback and verify recovery before resuming.
reasons: A 1% canary provides statistically useful latency signals in about 12 minutes.
Recent routing regressions appeared in error rate or p95 latency within four minutes, making automated canary gates effective.
Additive schema fields are safely ignored by the old application, so application rollback does not require a schema downgrade.
The routing feature flag offers faster mitigation than the nine-minute global application rollback.
A global-at-once deployment risks violating the five-minute customer error constraint, while waiting six weeks for staging would not eliminate third-party latency uncertainty.
assumptions: Feature-flag deactivation propagates quickly enough to prevent an error-rate breach from lasting more than five minutes.
Canary metrics are segmented from global metrics and include error rate, p95 latency, and database read-pattern health.
Regional promotion stages can be completed within one business day after the initial observation period.
The approved p95 latency threshold will be defined from current production baselines before rollout.
risks: Database read-pattern regressions cannot be fully mitigated by the routing flag and application rollback takes nine minutes.
A 1% canary may not expose region-specific or low-frequency failures, requiring regional stages and continued monitoring.
Poorly tuned automatic thresholds could cause false aborts or fail to detect subtle regressions.
Feature-flag propagation or observability delays could jeopardize the five-minute error-duration limit.

citations.claim: The previous three routing regressions were detectable through error rate or p95 latency within four minutes.
The schema changes are additive and remain compatible with rollback to the old application version.
A 1% canary yields useful latency signals in approximately 12 minutes.
Global application rollback takes nine minutes.
Production-identical staging would take six weeks and would still miss third-party latency variance.
A feature flag can disable the routing path without redeployment, but database read-pattern changes require application rollback.
